display.title: Tanya Shiur 22: Chapters 5 and 6, Torah as Food for the Soul and Zeh L'umas Zeh
display.summary_short: Two Yiddish Tanya sessions: chapter 5 on the unique union of Torah knowledge, and chapter 6 on the animal soul and the forces of kelipah, with stories of the Alter Rebbe and the Baal Shem Tov.
display.summary_long: Shiur 22 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series holds two sessions. The first completes Tanya chapter 5: when a person understands Torah, his mind both grasps and is enveloped by Hashem's wisdom, a union no other mitzvah reaches. The class explains 'Tov li toras picha' in the Chassidic way, and why Torah is called bread and food of the soul while mitzvos are its garments in Gan Eden. Two stories show how food shapes the soul: the Alter Rebbe traces a young scholar's spiritual decline to milk that was not chalav Yisroel, and the Baal Shem Tov leads his students into a forest to say l'chaim at the grave of a forced convert who brought a lost Jew back. The second session reviews chapters 1 to 5 and studies chapter 6: 'zeh l'umas zeh asah Elokim', the ten crowns of impurity, why the animal soul puts emotion before intellect, free choice, guarding thought, speech and action, and that holiness rests only where there is bittul. It closes with the Baal Shem Tov's blessing to a boy who would not move the tzaddik's shoes.
display.lesson: Torah learned with understanding unites a person with Hashem like nothing else, so guard what you eat, think, say and do, and choose the side of holiness.

study_text.note: Session 1 finishes chapter 5 (from 'V'zos maalah yeseirah'); session 2, starting at about 60:38, reviews chapters 1-5 and studies chapter 6.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 5: the unique union of knowing Torah
segments.summary: Torah understood with the mind unites a person with Hashem's wisdom, and it is the soul's food while mitzvos are its garments.

segments.title: The Alter Rebbe and the milk
segments.summary: The Alter Rebbe traces a young scholar's doubts in faith to milk that was not chalav Yisroel.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov's l'chaim in the forest
segments.summary: The Baal Shem Tov says l'chaim at the forest grave of a forced convert who helped a lost scholar return to Judaism.

segments.title: Chapters 1-5 in brief and a preview of chapter 6
segments.summary: The first session sums up the opening chapters and ends with a promise to continue chapter 6 next week.

segments.title: Second session: review of 'be a tzaddik, not a rasha'
segments.summary: A new session reviews why Tanya is the book of beinonim and what chapters 1-5 taught.

segments.title: Tanya chapter 6: zeh l'umas zeh asah Elokim
segments.summary: The animal soul's ten crowns and bad midos, free choice, guarding thought, speech and action, and bittul as the place where holiness rests.

segments.title: Young Moshe chooses between gold and coals
segments.summary: An angel guides baby Moshe's hand to the coals, an example of a choice between two things that look alike.

segments.title: The Baal Shem Tov's shoes
segments.summary: A boy who would not move the Baal Shem Tov's shoes was blessed with long life and is still young at 114.

segments.title: Closing: cleaving to Hashem
segments.summary: Guarding every thought and word brings a person close to Hashem, the source of life.
